findings.quote: by taking back a city that had often disputed control with them
findings.problem: ταύτην ἐπανελομένους = 'by destroying/doing away with' the city, not 'taking back'.
findings.proposed_fix: by destroying a city that had often disputed control with them

findings.quote: but arriving at the same end through the appearances they displayed
findings.problem: ἥξειν δ᾽ ἐπὶ ταὐτὸ τέλος ἐκ τῶν προφαινομένων = 'but would reach the same end, to judge from present indications' (future, a prediction), not a completed arrival 'through appearances they displayed'.
findings.proposed_fix: but bound, to judge from present indications, to reach the same end

findings.quote: For since nothing irreparable had happened on account of them, they had resolved in a harsh and irreversible way against them, willing to accept and endure anything in order to carry out what had been ordered.
findings.problem: μηδενὸς ... γεγονότος is concessive ('although the Carthaginians had done nothing irreparable'), and the genitive absolute πᾶν ἀναδεχομένων καὶ πᾶν ὑπομενόντων ποιήσειν τὸ προσταττόμενον refers to the Carthaginians (who accepted every condition and submitted to do whatever was ordered), not the Romans.
findings.proposed_fix: For although the Carthaginians had done nothing irreparable, the Romans had taken an irreparable and harsh decision against them, even though they accepted every condition and submitted to do whatever was ordered.

findings.quote: gradually revealing one demand and concealing another
findings.problem: τὰ μὲν προτείνοντες, τὰ δὲ παραγυμνοῦντες = 'putting forward some demands and disclosing others'; παραγυμνοῦντες means uncovering, not concealing (contrast ἐπικρυπτομένους earlier).
findings.proposed_fix: gradually putting forward one demand and disclosing another

findings.quote: for when the Carthaginians had handed themselves over, the Romans had simply done what they wished, since those surrendering were no longer obeying orders, and had thus brought necessity upon them
findings.problem: λαβόντας γὰρ τὴν ἐπιτροπὴν παρ᾽ ἑκόντων ὃ βούλοιντο πράττειν = 'having received from willing parties the authority to do what they wished'; the Romans received authority, they did not 'simply do what they wished'. οὐ πειθαρχούντων = 'when they did not obey' (no 'no longer').
findings.proposed_fix: for having received from the Carthaginians, of their own free will, the authority to do whatever they wished, the Romans, when the Carthaginians did not obey their orders, had thus brought compulsion to bear on them

units.note: μικροῦ δεῖν in the 'breach of faith' clause is awkwardly placed and its scope is uncertain; current English 'or even, scarcely, to breach of faith' preserves the ambiguity, left as is.

findings.quote: we no longer had any need at all
findings.problem: μηκέτι χρείαν ἡμῶν εἶναι μηδεμίαν = 'there was no longer any need of us at all' (Polybius was no longer needed), not that 'we' had no needs.
findings.proposed_fix: there was no longer any need of us at all

findings.quote: Prusias would arrive not only already dead, but that Nicomedes too would grow old in his kingdom before the embassy could ever get there
findings.problem: συμβήσεται μὴ μόνον ἀπολόμενον φθάσαι τὸν Προυσίαν = 'not only would Prusias be dead before they arrived' — Prusias is not the one arriving; the envoys are.
findings.proposed_fix: not only would Prusias be dead before the embassy arrived, but Nicomedes too would have grown old on his throne

findings.quote: but also to seek punishment from him
findings.problem: τιμωρίαν βούλεσθαι παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ λαμβάνειν = 'to wish to take vengeance on him'; the English can be read as the people wanting to be punished by him.
findings.proposed_fix: but also to wish to take vengeance on him

units.note: Opening clause (εἰδεχθὴς ... καίπερ ἐκ συλλογισμοῦ βελτίων ὑπάρχων) is doubtful in the transmitted text; current English is a defensible reading, not altered.

findings.quote: he preserved his whole life and left his kingdom free from every plot and every domestic stain
findings.problem: διετήρησε τὸν ὅλον βίον ... ἄμοιρον αὑτοῦ γενέσθαι τὴν βασιλείαν = 'throughout his whole life he kept his kingdom free from' plots; τὸν ὅλον βίον is duration, not the object 'preserved his life'.
findings.proposed_fix: he kept his kingdom, throughout his whole life, free from every plot and every domestic stain

findings.quote: extensive and fully fruitful estates in separate allotments
findings.problem: μυριοπλέθρους ἀγροὺς = estates of ten thousand plethra each; the number is smoothed into 'extensive'.
findings.proposed_fix: fully fruitful estates of ten thousand plethra each in separate allotments
